old: In a benzylic or allylic carbocation, the empty p orbital overlaps both the filled $\pi$ system (resonance) and filled $\alpha$ $C-H$ $\sigma$ orbitals (hyperconjugation)
new: In a benzylic or allylic carbocation, the empty p orbital overlaps the adjacent filled $\pi$ system (resonance); hyperconjugation with filled $\alpha$ $C-H$ $\sigma$ orbitals stabilises alkyl-substituted carbocations, e.g. $(CH_3)_3C^+$ with 9 $\alpha$-H, and a substituted benzylic or allylic cation carrying $\alpha$-H on an alkyl group can benefit from both
fixes: Benzyl and allyl cations are stabilised by resonance, not hyperconjugation
